summary: Today’s pulse tracks JD Vance casts doubt on firing squad execution and says he will not watch it, Homeland security secretary claims Mamdani’s comments after New York ICE shooting ‘incite hostility’ – US politics live, and Trump establishes committee to investigate Fed governor Lisa Cook. Across BBC, Guardian, and NPR, the strongest repeated signals are farage, firing, and trump. In the background, Parties prepare for byelection in Farage seat amid speculation over £5m gift inquiry and U.S. working to reverse an Egyptian man's third-country deportation to Africa keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: JD Vance casts doubt on firing squad execution and says he will not watch it
headlines.description: The planned execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad would be the first military execution in more than 60 years.

headlines.title: Homeland security secretary claims Mamdani’s comments after New York ICE shooting ‘incite hostility’ – US politics live
headlines.description: Markwayne Mullin addressed the Bronx shooting of a man in a car with a five-year-old present after New York’s mayor said ICE is ‘rotten to its core’ She added that “public executions are typically held in authoritarian countries to instil fear in the population, and to show the power and control of the government.”

headlines.title: Trump establishes committee to investigate Fed governor Lisa Cook
headlines.description: US president renews his efforts to oust Cook despite supreme court ruling that her firing was unconstitutional Donald Trump announced on Friday that he is establishing a committee to investigate Lisa Cook, the US Federal Reserve governor, over allegations that she committed mortgage fraud, renewing his efforts to oust her despite a June supreme court ruling that her earlier firing was unconstitutional. Trump said a committee will consult with justice department officials to decide whether there is “cause” for her removal. The White House will hold an in-person hearing on 5 November to consider the allegations against Cook, which will be closed to the public but transcribed and published. Cook will be able to submit a written statement to present her own evidence and will be subject to examination from White House and her own legal counsel.

headlines.title: Parties prepare for byelection in Farage seat amid speculation over £5m gift inquiry
headlines.description: Tories said to be ready to fight in Clacton, with standards investigation rumoured to be nearing its end Nigel Farage’s rivals are gearing up for a byelection in Clacton in the months ahead, amid speculation that the standards inquiry into his £5m gift is nearing a conclusion. Conservative sources said the party was ready to fight in Farage’s seat, although senior figures in the shadow cabinet are divided about whether it would be winnable, given Farage’s victory in a byelection over the summer .

headlines.title: U.S. working to reverse an Egyptian man's third-country deportation to Africa
headlines.description: The Trump administration's effort to return Ahmed Soliman to the U.S. come after an Arizona judge said his deportation violated due process.

headlines.title: Two Latvians arrested at RAF base in Cambridgeshire released on bail
headlines.description: Men found inside RAF Molesworth, used by US and Nato for intelligence, freed on strict conditions as police continue investigation Two Latvian men have been released on bail after being arrested at an RAF base in Cambridgeshire used by the US military and Nato. The two men, aged 32 and 26, were arrested at 2am on Thursday after they were discovered inside RAF Molesworth in Cambridgeshire, which is used by the US military and Nato for intelligence operations.

headlinePool.description: Several member states of the international tribunal, including the UK, say they "strongly disagree" with the sanctions.

headlinePool.title: Navi Pillay, former UN human rights chief, wins Nobel Peace Prize
headlinePool.description: Pillay is recognised for her "efforts to promote peace and international law", the Norwegian Nobel Committee says.

headlinePool.title: US immigration officials defend ICE agents who shot man in same car as child
headlinePool.description: Oscar Belgal, the 28-year-old man, survived the shooting and is now being held at a detention facility outside of New York, officials said.

headlinePool.title: Florida execution called off after DeSantis withdraws death warrant for first time
headlinePool.description: Governor halts execution of William Lee Thompson, after Christa Pike survived failed lethal injections Ron DeSantis cancelled a planned execution in the state on Friday, days before a 74-year-old man was due to be killed by lethal injection. The move – the first time Florida’s governor has withdrawn a death warrant in his nearly eight years in office – comes just over a week after the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee.

headlinePool.title: Russian search engine Yandex struggles after Ukrainian strikes on data centres
headlinePool.description: Often dubbed "Russia's Google", the tech firm admits customers may experience disruption to digital services due to the attacks.

headlinePool.title: Labour byelection win shows party starting to win back voters on left
headlinePool.description: Party now polling 15 points above Greens, who had been ahead of Labour before Keir Starmer resigned as PM Labour is starting to win back voters on the left who became disillusioned under Keir Starmer’s leadership, the party’s deputy leader has claimed after it saw off Zack Polanski and the Greens to win the Holborn and St Pancras byelection. Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali took 45% of a relatively low turnout to keep Starmer’s old north London seat for the party, pushing Polanski, who had stood for the party he leads, into second place on 33%.

headlinePool.title: Severe turbulence injures at least eight and forces emergency landing in Miami
headlinePool.description: Multiple hospitalized after Avianca flight from Medellín to New York had to divert to Miami due to strong turbulence At least eight people were injured when an Avianca flight encountered severe turbulence and had to make an emergency landing in Miami early on Friday. Miami-Dade fire rescue said one person was rushed to a trauma center with severe injuries while seven others were taken to area hospitals in ambulances.

headlinePool.title: Ed Davey faces growing revolt against leadership as senior Lib Dem MP quits
headlinePool.description: Treasury spokesperson Charlie Maynard reportedly resigned in attempt to unseat leader as party slips in polls Ed Davey is facing a growing revolt against his leadership of the Liberal Democrats, after the resignation of a senior frontbench figure on Friday. Charlie Maynard, the Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesperson, has resigned in an attempt to unseat Davey after months of frustration over concerns that the party is failing to cut through with voters, the Guardian understands.

headlinePool.title: Did Russia play by the rules in reporting lab worker's death?
headlinePool.description: A global treaty signed by 197 countries — including Russia — requires reporting any death that could be a sign of an outbreak to come.
